content.title: Message Relay
content.summary: Practice a short check-in text, together. Choose which parts your family would put in a message. Nothing gets sent.
content.objective: Practice building a short message that tells family you're safe and where you are.
content.facilitation: An adult reads each card aloud. This is a private text to family only. Ask everyone whether it belongs in a short check-in text, and why. Nothing is sent from this activity.

discussed_out_of_town_contact.text: Your household went over having an out-of-town contact.

activity.prompt: Does this go in our message?
activity.reminderQuestion: Who is your household's out-of-town contact?
activity.recapBody: Ready.gov suggests letting family know you are safe and where you are, with short messages like "I'm OK. At library." Ready Kids says texts may have an easier time getting through than phone calls, and: unless you are in danger, send a text. It also suggests one out-of-town contact for everyone. Who you're with and your battery level are helpful extras: that's SitPrep's suggestion, not an official rule.
